analysis:
The only change to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (hunks at base line 170 and head lines 170-174) is documentation. It updates the 'Last updated' date and adds a sentence saying a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a coordinator ack once accepted work and local response writes finish (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, performLifecycleDrain). I reviewed the two supplied head_text units (lines 323-951) for context. They contain only unchanged protocol reference material, including prefix-cache objects, heartbeat, backend_capacity, inference messages, attestation_response, and models_replace.

No code, key handling, encryption, attestation or authorization logic is altered. The new sentence concerns availability: shutdown or update with no session. It does not weaken the TB-002 drain/admission-closed semantics, because it applies only when no registered session exists, so there is no coordinator routing to fence. It also does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache posture, the T-053 grant/endpoint binding, or T-008 fail-closed encryption.

Open integration question: the changed drain sentence is documentation of Swift behavior in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, which is not supplied. I could not verify that the implementation matches the doc, for example that a lifecycle drain cannot be entered while a session is registered but not yet visible to the drain path. That is a documentation-versus-code accuracy risk, not a demonstrated regression. No finding is raised.
